name: kidney-filter
prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Finished Body School textbook illustration for children ages 11–13. White background, large bold navy sans-serif headings, pale blue rounded label panels, softly shaded anatomical art, friendly and non-gory. Blood vessels red and dark burgundy; urine pale yellow. No watermark or tiny text. SQUARE 1:1 composition. Exact title "Kidneys filter the blood". One large bean-shaped KIDNEY CUTAWAY, showing believable renal tissue and a central pale yellow collecting pelvis. At the kidney hilum, show THREE DISTINCT connections: red renal artery with an arrow pointing INTO kidney, labeled "Blood in"; burgundy renal vein with an arrow pointing OUT of kidney, labeled "Blood back to body"; pale yellow ureter leading DOWNWARD from collecting pelvis, with a downward arrow labeled "Urine out". The ureter must be separate from blood vessels, and no blood cells may enter it. Anatomical collecting spaces connect to ureter; blood vessels connect into tissue. At bottom, two simple pale-blue caption bands: "Needed water and useful materials return to blood" and "Waste and extra water become urine". Clear explanatory simplified diagram, not a detailed nephron drawing. All labels comfortably within image.

name: urine-route
prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Finished Body School textbook illustration for children ages 11–13. White background, large bold navy sans-serif headings, pale blue rounded label panels, softly shaded anatomical art, friendly and non-gory. Blood vessels red and dark burgundy; urine pale yellow. No watermark or tiny text. PORTRAIT 4:5 composition. Exact title "Follow the urine's path". Front-view simplified neutral torso outline without face, genitals or reproductive organs. Two reddish-brown kidneys high in abdomen at either side of spine just below faint lower ribs; patient's right kidney (viewer left) a little lower. Exactly TWO thin pale-yellow ureters, one from each kidney hilum, descend SEPARATELY and connect to the same pink bladder near pelvis. Exactly ONE urethra exits from bladder bottom and points downward, ending outside simplified outline. Yellow arrowheads INSIDE ureters point toward bladder, and inside urethra point out/down. No blood vessels in this picture. Clear labels with accurate leader lines: "Kidneys" to both, "Ureters" to both long tubes, "Bladder" to sac, "Urethra" to single exit tube. Distinguish ureters from urethra clearly. Whole pathway visible without overlap. No urinary tube joining kidney to kidney.

name: bladder-storage
prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Finished Body School textbook illustration for children ages 11–13. White background, large bold navy sans-serif headings, pale blue rounded label panels, softly shaded anatomical art, friendly and non-gory. Blood vessels red and dark burgundy; urine pale yellow. No watermark or tiny text. SQUARE 1:1 composition. Exact title "The bladder stores urine". Two side-by-side panels headed "Filling" and "Emptying". Each contains a simple anatomical cutaway of pink muscular bladder with EXACTLY TWO ureters entering at upper sides, and ONE urethra exiting bottom. Left filling panel: a larger expanded rounded bladder containing pale-yellow urine, yellow arrows DOWN the two ureters INTO bladder, and the urethra closed with no outward flow arrow. Right emptying panel: a smaller contracting bladder, inward arrows OUTSIDE muscular walls showing squeezing, and one large yellow urine-flow arrow DOWN through urethra. No upward arrows in ureters, no blood, no kidneys or reproductive organs. Label "Ureters" once with paired leader lines to left panel's incoming tubes, "Bladder wall" to pink muscular wall, and "Urethra" to bottom exit. Keep flow direction unambiguous and avoid arrows from urine into tissue.

name: water-balance
prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Finished Body School textbook illustration for children ages 11–13. White background, large bold navy sans-serif headings, pale blue rounded label panels, softly shaded anatomical art, friendly and non-gory. Blood vessels red and dark burgundy; urine pale yellow. No watermark or tiny text. WIDE 2:1 landscape composition. Exact title "Keeping water balanced". Two equal spacious panels. Left heading "Extra water: more urine". Right heading "Body needs water: less urine". Each panel shows the SAME pair of functioning kidneys with red blood entering and dark-burgundy blood returning to body, drawn as small distinct red arrows toward kidney and burgundy arrows away. Two pale-yellow ureters lead DOWN from kidney hilums to one simple illustrated measuring container, NOT a bladder: larger amount of pale-yellow urine in left container, much smaller amount in right container. The containers must be same size with identical unnumbered scale marks, no numbers or drinking targets. No connections from blood vessels into containers. Make difference in urine quantity clear by liquid level and flow amount; kidneys identical size and healthy in BOTH panels. Exact bottom shared caption "The kidneys keep filtering in both situations." No blue blood, no claims that urine production stops, no water bottles or drinking advice. Large legible headings and margins. Add a short subtitle under the main title: "Urine made over the same time".
